messages:
maria: Heads-up — I spotted a VPN route rewrite that is injecting a header with an email into requests for /v1/relay. Some of those requests are getting sampled and exported to analytics. Potential PII leak.

jon: Ugh. Do you have repro steps or a single example we can scrub and look at? :eyes:

maria: Repro is simple from our corp VPN. curl to internal proxy shows: `X-User-Ident: alice@example.com` in flight. I saw a couple of lines in the sampler output where body was attached. Example log (sanitized): `INFO relay: req_id=abc123 route=/v1/relay headers={..., X-User-Ident: alice@example.com} sampled=true body_attached=true`

ashwin: That explains the telemetry noise we've been seeing. Right now sampling is route-rate + global sampler. We don't have a per-route PII flag that forces body strip. We should avoid ad-hoc regex scrubbers for headers — brittle.

katie: Proposal: add route metadata `sensitive: true|false` in route config. If sensitive=true then sampler must set `export_body=false` and redact headers by default (field-level allowlist). Also expose a console UX toggle so product teams can opt-in to strict mode.

jon: Sounds good. Is there any case where we need bodies for debug on those routes? We can do temporary inspect flows with breakglass that write to ephemeral store not analytics.

ashwin: Agree. Implementation sketch: 1) route metadata + migration; 2) sampler check: if route.sensitive then sample_policy = {export_body: false, export_headers: allowlist}; 3) console: add `sensitivity` badge and an override button that triggers an auditable breakglass flow.

maria: Can we also add an automated detection to suggest sensitivity? E.g., if header set contains `@` or looks like email in >0.1% of requests over a day, flag the route as candidate. Avoid auto-flipping, just surface in dashboard.

ashwin: Good idea — we can add a new metric `route_pii_indicator_rate` (percentage of requests with high-entropy header values or email-like patterns). Alert if >0.05% and sampling_exposed_count > 0.

jon: Here's a quick config snippet for the route metadata (WIP):
```yaml
routes:
  - id: relay-v1
    path: /v1/relay
    sensitive: true  # runtime-only flag, defaults to false
    sampling:
      policy: route-aware
```

katie: UX notes: console should not let you flip sensitive -> false without two-step confirmation and a compliance tag. We also need a dashboard card that shows "sampled_with_body" count per route and a scrubbed-sample preview that redacts emails.

sre-bot: deploy: /services/relay updated (deploy id dpl-2026-02-12-03) — changed header rewrite behavior in PR #3210 by @devops.

maria: PR #3210 is likely the cause — it was a quick patch to propagate user-id for routing. That patch didn't consider analytics exports.

ashwin: Action items: katie -> create console UX ticket + mockups (ETA EOD), ashwin -> add metric and alert rule to telemetry (ETA tomorrow), jon -> add sampler check and route metadata enforcement (PR target end of week), maria -> provide a list of sample log lines and the affected request ids.

katie: I'll scope the mock and include breakglass flow copy for legal. :thumbsup:

jon: I'll draft the sampler change so it can be toggled behind a feature flag. We'll add unit tests that ensure export_body=false for sensitive routes.

maria: Thanks — I'm going to purge analytics of known sampled records we can identify and send the list to security/compliance. We should also backfill a quick search to find any other routes that may leak emails in headers.

ashwin: For visibility: add a single-row console alert "PII candidate detected" that links to the route and shows `route_pii_indicator_rate`. That will help owners remediate before samples leak.

maria: Cool. If anyone sees other headers with email patterns please drop them here. I'll update this thread with PR numbers and the purge ticket.

jon: Nice triage — thanks all.
